claim_result.expected_chamber_outcome:
In a chamber run where the Si115x VDD is swept while illumination and all other settings are held fixed (e.g., the validate_t_vis_1-style experiment, with vis_1 as the primary output), a calibrated measurement will show the following behavior:

• For VDD well below the datasheet minimum (≈0–1.4 V), vis_1 will read essentially zero or only small noise-like counts, indicating the device is not operating.
• As VDD approaches the lower end of the recommended range (around 1.5–1.6 V), vis_1 will transition from near-zero to its normal operating level over a relatively narrow voltage interval.
• For VDD within the recommended operating range (1.62 V up to the top of the chamber sweep, ≈3.0 V), vis_1 will remain approximately constant (apart from measurement noise), with no strong systematic dependence on VDD.
• The chamber dataset only sweeps VDD up to about 3 V, so it will directly confirm the effective lower bound near 1.6 V and show stable operation up to 3 V, but it will not probe the 3.0–3.6 V portion of the datasheet range. If that region were tested, the expectation is that vis_1 would continue to behave similarly, remaining stable until close to the absolute-maximum rating is approached.

claim_result.reason: The datasheet states on the front page that the Si115x includes "dual 23-bit analog-to-digital converters" (p.1), which applies to all photodiode channels, including the visible channel. Later, the ADCPOSTx register description specifies that samples can be output either as "16-bit unsigned integer" or "24-bit signed integer" (p.44), and the ALS/proximity sections state that an overflow in 24-bit mode is reported as 0x7FFFFF (pp.8–9), which corresponds to a maximum usable code of 8,388,607 counts, consistent with a 23‑bit magnitude. Thus, the effective ADC bit depth for the visible channel envelope is 23 bits, giving a code range of 0 to 2^23−1 counts before saturation when configured for full-resolution 24‑bit output. While the datasheet never writes this range explicitly in decimal, it is directly implied by the stated 23‑bit ADC resolution and the 0x7FFFFF overflow code. No additional operating conditions are attached specifically to the ADC resolution beyond the general device context.

A 23-bit ADC yields 2^23 = 8,388,608 possible codes, with maximum non-overflow code 2^23−1 = 8,388,607, matching 0x7FFFFF. This applies equally to the visible channel because it uses the same ADC with a different photodiode mux setting.
